_about: Schema example for build_ad.mjs. Every URL, clip symbol and line of text is a PLACEHOLDER - replace all of them with the confirmed brand's clips and claims. Shape: a 20s VO-led Problem -> Solution ad, 9:16.

_schema.output: path for the rendered MP4, relative to this file. Default out/ad.mp4. With --draft the file gets a -draft suffix.
_schema.aspect: "9:16" (1080x1920) or "16:9" (1920x1080). Caption size and side margins adapt automatically.
_schema.width/height: only to force an off-spec size; set both.
_schema.fps: default 30. Every segment is normalised to this.
_schema.targetDuration: 15, 20, 25 or custom. The builder warns if the render misses by >0.5s.
_schema.fit: cover | contain | blurfill - default cover. Portrait UGC: cover in 9:16, blurfill in 16:9. Landscape clips in 9:16: cover + anchorX (one subject) or blurfill.
_schema.cacheDir: downloads and normalised segments are cached here. Default .adcache
_schema.workDir: scratch dir, wiped each run. Default .adwork. On Windows use a SHORT path like C:/adwork.
_schema.segmentCache: default true - reuse normalised segments across renders. false forces a full re-encode.
_schema.draft: true (or the --draft flag) renders half size with a fast encode for approval and the critic.
_schema.fontsDir: the brand cache's fonts/ folder, so captions use the brand face.

segments[].url | file: clip downloadUrl, rawVideoDownloadUrl, or a local path (a Remotion render, a user upload)
segments[].in / out: seconds into the source. Always set them.
segments[].anchorX / anchorY: where a cover-crop sits: 0 = left/top, 0.5 = centre (default), 1 = right/bottom. Check the subject stays in the crop from in to out.
segments[].move: pushin | pullback | glideleft | glideright | glideup | glidedown - motion without a cut.
segments[].transition: how this segment ENTERS: "cut" (default) or {type, duration}. Types: fade, dissolve, fadeblack, fadewhite, swipe*, smooth*, wipe*, reveal*, cover*, circleopen, circleclose, radial, zoomin, squeezeh, squeezev, pixelize, hblur. Directions: left/right/up/down.
segments[].audioLead: J-cut: seconds this segment's audio starts before its picture. Needs keepClipAudio true.
segments[].audioTail: L-cut: seconds this segment's audio continues after its picture ends. Needs keepClipAudio true.

audio.music: { file, duck (true), duckDb (-9), fadeOut (1.0), offsetDb (-4) }. Leave gainDb out: the builder measures voice and bed (EBU R128) and places the bed offsetDb under the voice.
audio.keepClipAudio: default false. false for every VO-led cut; true for testimonial, mashup and mixed A-roll ads.
audio.sfx: [{ name (a file in assets/sfx without .wav) | file, at (output seconds), gainDb (default -6) }] - CC0 effects mixed under the voice.

captions[].start / end: seconds on the OUTPUT timeline (the builder prints it - transitions shorten it)
captions[].text | lines: 4-5 words visible at once; lines[] + stagger for an ordered list
captions[].band: upper | middle | lower - pick per shot so it clears faces, the product and burned-in text
captions[].anim: fadeup (fade+rise, default) | fadedown (fade+drop) | pop (scale-pop) | punch (the one main claim) | slideleft/slideright (+ lines and stagger = slide-in-sequence) | fade | none
captions[].y: exact vertical position, 0 = top, 1 = bottom (clamped 0.08-0.88) - use instead of band when a band would sit on a face or the product.

_schema.captionStyle: { font, fontSize, primary, outline, outlineWidth, bold } - from brand.json or the user's guidelines. Default font is the bundled Poppins.
_schema.approvedClaims: figures the USER supplied this session (e.g. "30% off this week") - gate.mjs only lets numbers on screen that are in the website claims or here.
_schema.overlays[]: { file (a transparent ProRes 4444 .mov from the Remotion template's Overlay composition), at (output seconds) } - graphics laid over the footage, under the captions.

_timeline: Output = sum of clip durations - sum of transition durations. Here: 3.2 + 3.0 + 4.9 + 6.0 + 4.15 = 21.25s of clips, minus 0.25 + 0.5 + 0.5 = 1.25s of transitions = 20.0s. Time captions against the timeline the builder prints.

segments._beat: HOOK - the problem, shown (Actor B-roll or No Actor)
PIVOT - the one match cut: same action and framing as BBB, now with the product
SOLUTION + PROOF - the product doing its job
segments._why: Solution half: slower, smoother, a push-in.

segments._beat: CTA - product hero or end card
